name: 乾為天
judgment: Qian: primal origin, smooth unfolding, benefit, and steadfast correctness.
tuan: Great is the origin of Qian: all things owe their beginning to it, and it governs heaven. Clouds move and rain is bestowed; the many kinds of beings flow into their forms. Great clarity marks out end and beginning; the six places are completed each in its season, and season by season it rides six dragons to drive heaven. The way of Qian changes and transforms so that each being rectifies its nature and allotted life; preserving and uniting the great harmony brings benefit and steadfastness. It rises first among the multitude of creatures, and all states are peaceful and at rest.
xiang: Heaven moves with strength; the noble one strengthens himself without stopping. “The hidden dragon is not to be used”: yang is still below. “The dragon appears in the field”: virtue spreads everywhere. “All day he is active, active”: he keeps returning to the Way. “Perhaps it leaps from the depths”: to advance brings no blame. “The flying dragon is in heaven”: the great person is at work. “The overreaching dragon has regret”: fullness cannot last. Using nine: the virtue of heaven cannot be made the head.

lines.text: A hidden dragon: do not act.
lines.image: A hidden dragon not to be used: yang is still below.

lines.text: The dragon appears in the field; it is beneficial to see a great person.
lines.image: The dragon appears in the field: virtue spreads everywhere.

lines.text: The noble one is active all day, and at dusk stays alert as if in danger; no blame.
lines.image: All day active, active: he keeps returning to the Way.

lines.text: Perhaps leaping, still within the depths: no blame.
lines.image: Leaping within the depths: advancing brings no blame.

lines.text: A flying dragon in heaven; it is beneficial to see a great person.
lines.image: A flying dragon in heaven: the great person is at work.

lines.text: An overreaching dragon has regret.
lines.image: An overreaching dragon has regret: what is full cannot last.

core: Vigorous, upright creative power brings growth and smooth success, but excess strength invites reversal.
plain: This is a time of strong initiative, clear timing, and rising capacity. Act with discipline and keep checking the limits of your power; when influence peaks, restraint matters more than force.
advice: Use your strength, but stop before force turns into overreach.

name: 坤為地
summary: Supple yielding strength, broadly bearing all
judgment: Kun: primal success. It is beneficial to keep the steadfastness of a mare. If the noble person has somewhere to go, he loses the way at first and afterward finds a master. It is beneficial to gain friends in the southwest and to lose friends in the northeast. Quiet steadfastness brings good fortune.
tuan: Perfect is the origin of Kun: all things owe their birth to it, and it obediently receives heaven. Kun is deep and carries all beings; its virtue joins with the boundless. It contains, enlarges, and makes radiant, so every kind of being flourishes. The mare belongs to the earth and travels the earth without limit: supple, compliant, beneficial, steadfast. Where the noble one goes, to go first is to lose the way; to follow after is to find the constant. In the southwest one gains friends and moves with one’s own kind; in the northeast one loses friends, yet in the end there is celebration. The good fortune of quiet steadfastness answers to earth’s boundlessness.
xiang: The condition of earth is receptive; the noble one carries all beings with ample virtue.

lines.text: Treading on frost: hard ice is coming.
lines.image: Treading frost, then hard ice: yin begins to congeal; following that course leads to solid ice.

lines.text: Straight, square, and great: without practice, nothing is not beneficial.
lines.image: The movement of six in the second place is straight through squareness; without practice and without disadvantage, the way of earth is radiant.

lines.text: Concealing brilliance, one may remain steadfast. If serving the king’s affairs, claim no completion, but there will be an end.
lines.image: Concealing brilliance yet able to stand firm: it issues forth in its season. Serving the king’s affairs: understanding shines broadly.

lines.text: Tie the sack shut: no blame, no praise.
lines.image: A tied sack, no blame: carefulness prevents harm.

lines.text: A yellow lower garment: supreme good fortune.
lines.image: A yellow lower garment, supreme good fortune: patterned beauty is held within.

lines.text: Dragons battle in the wilds; their blood is dark and yellow.
lines.image: Dragons battle in the wilds: their way is exhausted.

core: Receptive stillness can bear great weight, but restless self-assertion breaks the pattern.
plain: Do not force direction now; support, contain, and complete what is already underway. Choose allies by affinity and timing, not by ambition. Staying steady and dependable turns limitation into strength.
advice: Follow the reliable lead; bear the load without competing for control.

name: 水雷屯
judgment: Tun: great success, benefit, and steadfastness. Do not use this to set out anywhere; it is beneficial to establish lords.
tuan: Tun is when hard and soft first join and difficulty is born: movement inside danger, yet great success through correctness. Thunder and rain move and fill everything; heaven creates the dim beginnings. It is fitting to establish lords, yet not to rest in ease.
xiang: Clouds and thunder mass together: difficulty at the beginning. The noble one orders and unravels the tangled threads.

lines.text: Halted and turning back, it is beneficial to dwell in steadfastness and to establish lords.
lines.image: Though halted and turning, the will moves rightly; the noble lowers himself to the lowly and greatly wins the people.

lines.text: Difficulty upon difficulty, mounted horses wheel and turn. Not raiders but suitors; the woman remains true and does not consent—after ten years she consents.
lines.image: The hardship of six in the second place: it rides above the hard line. She consents only after ten years: a return to the normal.

lines.text: Chasing the deer with no forester, one only enters the forest. The noble one sees the turning point—better to let it go; to pursue brings distress.
lines.image: Chasing deer without a guide is simply letting the quarry run; the noble one abandons it. To go on brings distress and a dead end.

lines.text: Mounted horses wheel and turn; seeking marriage, go forward—good fortune, nothing unfavorable.
lines.image: To seek and then go is clarity.

lines.text: Hoarding the rich gift: in small matters steadfastness is lucky; in great matters it is ominous.
lines.image: Hoarding the rich gift: the giving has not shone widely.

lines.text: Mounted horses wheel and turn; tears of blood fall in a stream.
lines.image: Tears of blood streaming: how could this last?

core: Birth is powerful but obstructed; effort first, ease later.
plain: The situation is promising but still tangled, so do not rush travel or expansion. Build structure, appoint capable people, and expect delay before momentum becomes usable.
advice: Organize support first; postpone travel and appoint capable local leaders.

name: 山水蒙
summary: Ignorance seeks teaching and timely guidance
judgment: Meng: success. It is not I who seek the foolish child; the foolish child seeks me. At the first divination I answer; asking again and again is disrespect, and when disrespected I do not answer. It is beneficial to be steadfast.
tuan: Meng: beneath the mountain lies danger; meeting danger and stopping is folly. That Meng succeeds is because success moves in accord with the time and strikes the mean. “It is not I who seek the foolish child; the foolish child seeks me”: the wills respond. “At the first inquiry I answer”: hardness holds the center. Asking again and again is disrespect; when disrespected I do not answer, because pestering insults the state of not-knowing. To nourish correctness within ignorance is the work of a sage.
xiang: A spring rises beneath the mountain: youthful folly. The noble one makes action decisive and nourishes virtue.

lines.text: Opening ignorance: it helps to use correction and to remove shackles; pushing on brings trouble.
lines.image: It helps to use correction in order to set the standard right.

lines.text: Embracing the ignorant brings good fortune. Taking a wife brings good fortune; the son can manage the household.
lines.image: The son can keep the house: hard and soft join.

lines.text: Do not marry the woman who sees a wealthy man and loses hold of herself; nothing is beneficial.
lines.image: Do not take such a woman: her conduct is not compliant.

lines.text: Trapped in ignorance: distress.
lines.image: The distress of being trapped in ignorance: alone and far from what is solid.

lines.text: A child’s ignorance: good fortune.
lines.image: The good fortune of a child’s ignorance: it follows and yields.

lines.text: Strike at ignorance: it is not good to act as a robber; it is good to ward off robbers.
lines.image: It helps to ward off violence: above and below are in accord.

core: Understanding is still closed; guidance works only when sought sincerely and used decisively.
plain: Admit what is not yet known and let the question come to the teacher, not the reverse. Give a clear answer once, correct gently, and refuse to reward pestering or evasion. Firm education and practiced character gradually open the spring under the mountain.
advice: Answer sincere questions once; refuse repeated demands for easy certainty.

name: 水天需
judgment: Waiting. If you have sincerity, you will be radiant and successful. Perseverance brings good fortune. It is favorable to cross the great river.
tuan: Waiting means waiting, because danger lies ahead. Strength and vigor do not sink into danger, so their meaning is never confined or exhausted. Waiting with sincerity brings radiance and success; perseverance brings good fortune. Standing in the heavenly position means occupying the central place of correctness. It is favorable to cross the great river, for going forward brings achievement.
xiang: Clouds rise into the sky: this is Waiting. Thus the superior person maintains nourishment through food and drink and finds ease in companionship.

lines.text: Waiting in the outskirts. It is beneficial to persist steadily; there is no blame.
lines.image: Waiting in the outskirts means not entering danger. Persisting steadily and without blame shows that nothing has departed from the proper way.

lines.text: Waiting on the sands. There may be some criticism, but the end is good.
lines.image: Waiting on the sands means one remains midway. Although there may be slight criticism, it ends in good fortune.

lines.text: Waiting in the mud invites bandits to come.
lines.image: Waiting in the mud means danger lies outside. By drawing attackers toward oneself, one avoids defeat through caution and care.

lines.text: Waiting amid blood; one comes out of the pit.
lines.image: Waiting amid blood means yielding and listening to necessity.

lines.text: Waiting with wine and food. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.image: Waiting with wine and food brings good fortune through moderation and correctness.

lines.text: One enters the pit, and unexpected guests arrive, three in all. Respecting them ends in good fortune.
lines.image: When unexpected guests arrive, respecting them ends in good fortune. Although one does not occupy the proper position, no great failure has occurred.

core: Danger lies ahead, so pressing forward would be unwise. Hold to what is right, wait patiently, and let the proper opportunity arrive.
plain: Waiting asks you to remain still while conditions are not yet favorable. Keep your purpose clear, preserve your integrity, and prepare for the right opening rather than forcing it. Steady patience can lead to eventual progress and success.
advice: Hold your position, prepare carefully, and wait for the proper opening.

name: 天水訟
judgment: Conflict. If you have sincerity, be restrained and alert. Mid-course is favorable, but the end is bad. It is beneficial to see a great person; it is not favorable to cross the great river.
tuan: Conflict: when the upper is strong and the lower is dangerous, meeting danger with vigor creates conflict. In conflict, sincerity, restraint, and alertness make the middle course favorable, because the strong approach finds its proper center. The end is bad, for conflict cannot be completed successfully. It is beneficial to see a great person, because that honors moderation and correctness. It is not favorable to cross the great river, for one would fall into the abyss.
xiang: Heaven and water move in opposite directions: this is Conflict. Thus the superior person begins all undertakings with careful planning.

lines.text: Do not continue the matter. There may be slight criticism, but the end is good.
lines.image: Not continuing the matter means conflict cannot be prolonged. Although there may be small criticisms, their arguments can still be clarified.

lines.text: Unable to prevail in the dispute, one withdraws and flees. Even the people of the three hundred households of his town suffer no blame.
lines.image: Unable to prevail in the dispute, one withdraws and runs away. When those below dispute those above, trouble comes upon the one who initiates it.

lines.text: Eating the old blessings. Perseverance is difficult, but the end is good. If one follows the king’s affairs, he does not claim achievement.
lines.image: Eating the old blessings is good when one follows what is above.

lines.text: Unable to prevail in the dispute, one returns and accepts his place, becoming peaceful and upright. This is good.
lines.image: Returning and accepting one’s place means becoming peaceful and upright without losing what is right.

lines.text: In conflict, there is supreme good fortune.
lines.image: The good fortune of conflict comes through moderation and correctness.

lines.text: Perhaps a decorated belt is granted, but it is stripped away three times before the day is over.
lines.image: Receiving blessings through conflict is still insufficient to inspire reverence.

core: When circumstances pull people in opposite directions, disputes become likely. Avoid letting conflict harden, seek fair mediation, and do not pursue a struggle beyond its proper limits.
plain: This hexagram warns that competition can become destructive even when each side believes it has a case. Restrain the dispute early, appeal to impartial authority, and avoid risky action while emotions are high. A measured settlement is better than a complete victory.
advice: Stop the dispute early and seek a fair, impartial settlement.

name: 地水師
judgment: The Army. Perseverance is favorable. An experienced commander brings good fortune and no blame.
tuan: The Army means an multitude, and correctness means setting them right. Those who can set a multitude right may rule. Strong at the center and responsive to one another, they move through danger with ease. They use this force to bring order to the world, and the people follow them. How could such an undertaking be anything but good and blameless?
xiang: Water lies within the earth: this is The Army. Thus the superior person is broad in his care for the people and gathers them together.

lines.text: An army must be dispatched under regulations. If they are not good, it is bad.
lines.image: Dispatching an army under regulations is favorable; departing from them is bad.

lines.text: Within the army, the middle course is favorable and there is no blame. The king grants commands three times.
lines.image: The middle course within the army is favorable because it receives Heaven’s favor. The king’s repeated grants of command embrace all the nations.

lines.text: The army may return with bodies on its carts: this is bad.
lines.image: If the army returns bearing corpses, it has achieved nothing great.

lines.text: The army withdraws to the left. There is no blame.
lines.image: Withdrawing to the left is blameless because it does not depart from the proper way.

lines.text: There are birds in the field; it is beneficial to capture them. The words offer no blame. The eldest son leads the army, while younger men bring back corpses. Perseverance is bad.
lines.image: The eldest son leads the army because he acts with moderation. Younger men bring back the army because their command is misassigned.

lines.text: The ruler issues commands, establishing a state and passing on a family. Do not employ petty people.
lines.image: The ruler’s command recognizes and rewards proper achievement. Employing petty people would certainly disorder the state.

core: Collective action succeeds when it is united by justice, clear command, and proper conduct. Without discipline and responsibility, even a worthy cause can turn disastrous.
plain: The Army represents organized effort and the use of many people toward a common end. Success depends on a clear objective, disciplined conduct, and leaders who bear responsibility. Mobilize people only for a cause that can command their genuine support.
advice: Organize people around a clear goal and enforce disciplined conduct.

name: 水地比
judgment: Holding Together is good. If you return to the original oracle and seek it again, you will have lasting perseverance and no blame. When unrest has stilled, those who come will be welcome. The one who comes late is bad.
tuan: Holding Together is good. Holding together means assistance: those below are obedient. Return to the original oracle and seek it again; through lasting perseverance, there is no blame, because of the firm strength within. When unrest has stilled, the upper and lower respond to one another. The one who comes late is bad, because his way has reached its end.
xiang: Water flows over the earth: this is Holding Together. Thus the ancient kings established the ten thousand states and brought the feudal lords into closer bonds.

lines.text: There is sincerity in joining. There is no blame. Sincerity fills the vessel, and in the end there is also good fortune.
lines.image: At the beginning of holding together, there is good fortune to come from an unexpected source.

lines.text: Hold together from within. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.image: Holding together from within means not losing one’s proper nature.

lines.text: Hold together with the wrong person.
lines.image: Holding together with the wrong person must also cause harm.

lines.text: Hold together outwardly. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.image: Holding together outwardly with the worthy means following what is above.

lines.text: Holding together is manifest. The king hunts but allows three directions to remain open, losing the game that runs ahead. The people of the town need not be warned, and this is good.
lines.image: The good fortune of manifest union comes from correct placement and moderation. By rejecting what turns against him and accepting what accords with him, the king loses the game that runs ahead. The people need no warning because the ruler acts with moderation.

lines.text: Holding together without a beginning brings bad fortune.
lines.image: Holding together without a beginning has no proper end.

core: People flourish when they unite with trust and support one another from the beginning. Last-minute attachment, without genuine commitment, cannot sustain the relationship.
plain: Holding Together describes alliance, cooperation, and mutual support. Begin relations sincerely, confirm their basis through repeated consultation, and make room for others to join before things have settled. Delayed or insincere participation weakens the whole.
advice: Build trust early and welcome others with consistent sincerity.

name: 風天小畜
judgment: Small Taming: Success. Dense clouds gather, but no rain falls; they drift in from the west beyond the city.
tuan: Small Taming: The yielding line holds its proper place, and the lines above and below respond to it; this is called Small Taming. Because the strong line is balanced and centered while the yielding line carries out its purpose, there is success. The dense clouds do not bring rain because their movement is still directed upward. They drift from the west beyond the city because their movement has not yet begun.
xiang: The wind moves across the sky: this is Small Taming. Thus the noble person cultivates refined literary accomplishments and virtue.

lines.text: Returning by the proper path, what fault could there be? Good fortune.
lines.image: Returning by the proper path is auspicious because its meaning is right.

lines.text: One is drawn back to the proper path. Good fortune.
lines.image: Being drawn back to the proper path at the center means one does not lose oneself.

lines.text: The axle-shaft comes loose from the wheel, and husband and wife turn against each other.
lines.image: Husband and wife turn against each other because they cannot correct the disorder in the household.

lines.text: Keeping faith, the blood is cleared away and the danger departs. No fault.
lines.image: With faith and the danger removed, one joins in agreement with those above.

lines.text: Keeping faith and holding fast, sharing wealth with the neighboring people.
lines.image: Keeping faith and holding fast means one does not become wealthy alone.

lines.text: The rain has fallen and the clouds have dispersed. Now the virtue that sustains all things can be borne. The woman remains steadfast but in danger. As the moon nears full, the noble person's journey brings misfortune.
lines.image: With the rain fallen and the clouds dispersed, accumulated virtue can sustain all things. The noble person's journey is unfortunate because there is still something to be uncertain about.

core: Strength is limited and progress is restrained. Keep your abilities ready, wait for the right moment, and advance patiently rather than forcing the situation.
plain: Small Taming suggests success, but the rain is still being held back. Like dense clouds that have not yet released their rain, your plans may gather force before they can produce results. Move carefully, preserve your resources, and wait for conditions that allow your efforts to come to fruition.
advice: Build your strength and wait patiently for the proper moment to move.

name: 天澤履
judgment: Treading: One treads on the tiger's tail, yet the tiger does not bite. Success.
tuan: Treading: The yielding line treads on the strong line. It is joyful and responds to Qian; therefore, though one treads on the tiger's tail, the tiger does not bite, and there is success. The strong line is balanced and correct; when it occupies the supreme position, it feels no guilt, for it is bright and honorable.
xiang: Heaven above and the marsh below: this is Treading. Thus the noble person distinguishes the upper and lower orders and settles the people's aspirations.

lines.text: One walks in plain shoes. No fault.
lines.image: Walking in plain shoes means going alone according to one's own resolve.

lines.text: The path underfoot is level and open. For the secluded person, steadfastness brings good fortune.
lines.image: The secluded person is steadfast and fortunate because the center of his being is not disordered.

lines.text: The one-eyed can see; the lame can walk. One treads on the tiger's tail, and the tiger bites. Misfortune. A warrior defies the ruler.
lines.image: The one-eyed can see, but this is not enough for clear perception. The lame can walk, but is not fit to travel with others. The misfortune of being bitten comes from occupying an improper position. A warrior defies the ruler because his resolve is overly forceful.

lines.text: One treads on the tiger's tail, fearful and trembling, and ultimately brings good fortune.
lines.image: Fearful and trembling ultimately brings good fortune because one's resolve continues to move forward.

lines.text: One treads boldly and decisively. Steadfastness, but danger.
lines.image: Bold, decisive treading remains in danger because the position is appropriate.

lines.text: One examines the steps and considers their signs. Turning back brings great good fortune.
lines.image: Great good fortune at the highest position brings great celebration.

core: Every step carries the risk of danger, yet careful conduct can keep you safe. Approach power with humility, caution, and respect for proper roles.
plain: Treading warns that even a small step can place you in danger, like placing your foot on a tiger's tail. Success depends on conduct that is humble, balanced, and careful. Respect the structure around you and let steady, proper behavior make the danger pass.
advice: Move cautiously, respect proper roles, and let humility guide every step.

name: 地天泰
judgment: Peace: The small departs and the great arrives. Good fortune and success.
tuan: Peace: The small departs and the great arrives; there is good fortune and success. This means that heaven and earth interact, so all things communicate; those above and below interact, so their aims are united. The inner lines are yang and the outer lines are yin; within is strength, without is compliance; within are noble people and without are lesser people. The way of the noble person grows, while the way of the lesser person declines.
xiang: Heaven and earth interact: this is Peace. The ruler therefore completes the way of heaven and earth, assists and complements what is fitting in heaven and earth, and thereby helps the people.

lines.text: Pull up the weeds; their roots come with them. It is auspicious to move forward.
lines.image: Pulling up the weeds and moving forward is auspicious because the resolve reaches outward.

lines.text: One embraces the vastness, crosses the river without boat or oar, and leaves no one behind. Friends are lost, yet one upholds the central way.
lines.image: Embracing the vastness and crossing by the central way brings greater brilliance.

lines.text: Nothing is level that does not become sloping; nothing goes out that does not return. Preserving righteousness through hardship brings no fault. Do not worry about sincerity; there will be blessings in your food.
lines.image: What goes out returns, just as the boundary between heaven and earth works in this way.

lines.text: One flutters about, not enriching oneself by taking from the neighbors, and does not warn others through sincerity.
lines.image: Fluttering about without enriching oneself shows that all have lost their substance. Not warning others through sincerity means the intention at the center is to be free from concern.

lines.text: King Yi of Zhou gave his daughter in marriage. This brings great good fortune.
lines.image: Great good fortune through blessings comes from acting in accordance with the central way and one's intention.

lines.text: The city walls fall into the moats. Do not use the army. Announce orders from the city and maintain steadfastness, but there will be difficulty.
lines.image: When the city walls fall into the moats, the command has become disordered.

core: This is a time of exchange, communication, and shared prosperity. When differences meet and cooperate, different strengths can create harmony, though lasting peace still requires responsibility.
plain: Peace describes a favorable meeting of opposites: the small recedes and the great advances, while those above and below find common ground. Cooperation is possible because strengths can complement one another rather than compete. Preserve the harmony by acting fairly, supporting others, and sharing the resulting benefits.
advice: Build cooperation, communicate openly, and share the benefits fairly.

name: 天地否
judgment: Standstill: Obstruction is not for the right person. It is unfavorable for the noble person to remain steadfast; the great departs and the small arrives.
tuan: Standstill: Obstruction is not for the right person. It is unfavorable for the noble person to remain steadfast; the great departs and the small arrives. This means that heaven and earth do not interact, so all things are blocked; those above and below do not interact, so there is no unified realm under heaven. Within is yin and without is yang; within is yielding and without is strong; within are lesser people and without are noble people. The way of the lesser person grows, while the way of the noble person declines.
xiang: Heaven and earth do not interact: this is Standstill. Thus the noble person conserves virtue to avoid hardship and refuses the honor of official salary.

lines.text: Pull up the weeds; their roots come with them. Steadfastness brings good fortune and success.
lines.image: Pulling up the weeds and remaining steadfast is auspicious because the resolve is directed toward the ruler.

lines.text: One embraces and receives. For the lesser person this is good fortune; for the great person it is obstruction, yet there is success.
lines.image: For the great person, obstruction still permits success because one does not disorder the community.

lines.text: One embraces shame.
lines.image: Embracing shame is the result of occupying an improper position.

lines.text: One has a mandate; there is no fault. How does anyone share in its blessings?
lines.image: Having a mandate and remaining without fault means that the resolve can be carried out.

lines.text: Restrain the obstruction. For the great person this is good fortune. Keep saying, “I shall be lost; I shall be lost,” and one will be bound to the sturdy mulberry tree.
lines.image: The great person's good fortune comes from occupying the proper position.

lines.text: Overturn the obstruction. Obstruction comes first, and joy comes afterward.
lines.image: When obstruction reaches its end, it is overturned; it cannot last forever.

core: Communication is blocked and influence is turning toward lesser concerns. Preserve your principles, avoid entanglement in power, and wait for a more constructive situation.
plain: Standstill describes a failure of exchange between heaven and earth and between people above and below. The right course is no longer favored, while lesser interests gain ground. Keep your conduct restrained and principled, avoid seeking status or advantage in a disordered environment, and preserve your ability to act when conditions improve.
advice: Conserve your virtue and avoid pursuing status while communication remains blocked.

name: 天火同人
summary: People unite above and below in shared purpose
judgment: Fellowship: fellowship in the open field brings success. It is favorable to cross the great river and favorable for a person of integrity to remain steadfast.
tuan: In Fellowship, the yielding line gains its proper place, holds the center, and responds to Heaven; this is called Fellowship. Fellowship means: fellowship in the open field brings success, and it is favorable to cross the great river; this is Heaven moving forward. Bright and strong, centered and correct, and met by response: this is the uprightness of the person of integrity. Only the person of integrity can penetrate and unite the aims of all under heaven.
xiang: Heaven together with fire: Fellowship. The person of integrity groups people by kind and distinguishes things by their nature.

lines.text: Fellowship at the gate: no blame.
lines.image: Going out through the gate to join others—who could find fault with that?

lines.text: Fellowship only within the clan: regret.
lines.image: Fellowship only within the clan is a path that ends in regret.

lines.text: Armed men are hidden in the brush; he climbs the high ridge, yet for three years he cannot rise.
lines.image: Hiding troops in the brush means the opponent is strong. Not rising for three years means the peaceful course is the way.

lines.text: He mounts the wall but cannot carry the attack: good fortune.
lines.image: He climbs the wall, but rightfulness keeps him from prevailing. The good fortune is that, cornered, he returns to the rule.

lines.text: In fellowship there is first weeping and crying, then laughter. Great armies conquer and meet.
lines.image: Before fellowship there is weeping because the heart is centered and straight. Great armies meet means each side must overcome the other.

lines.text: Fellowship in the outskirts: no regret.
lines.image: Fellowship in the outskirts means the aim has not yet been reached.

core: This is a time for people to come together around a common aim. Agreement reaches farther when it is public and principled, not confined to a private circle.
plain: The situation favors cooperation that is open to everyone, not cliquish loyalty. Move forward with allies, keep your motives clean, and stay steady. Broad fellowship can carry a heavy undertaking across difficulty.
advice: Build support in the open; do not rely only on your own camp.

name: 火天大有
summary: Abundance held in step with heaven's timing
judgment: Great Possession: supreme success.
tuan: In Great Possession, the yielding line obtains the honored place, holds the great center, and is answered from above and below; this is called Great Possession. Its power is strong and bright, it responds to heaven and moves with the season; therefore there is supreme success.
xiang: Fire above the heavens: Great Possession. The person of integrity suppresses evil and raises up good, obeys heaven, and cherishes its mandate.

lines.text: No entangling harm; not a fault. If you keep to what is difficult and demanding, there is no blame.
lines.image: At the first nine of Great Possession, there is no entangling harm.

lines.text: A great wagon is loaded; there is somewhere to go, no blame.
lines.image: A great wagon carrying the load gathers the weight in the center and does not fail.

lines.text: A prince offers sacrifice to the Son of Heaven; a petty person cannot do this.
lines.image: A prince offering to the Son of Heaven would be harmed by a petty person.

lines.text: He does not swell with his plenty: no blame.
lines.image: Not swelling with plenty brings no blame because he sees clearly and distinguishes plainly.

lines.text: His sincerity comes in exchange, and there is dignity: good fortune.
lines.image: His sincerity coming in exchange means trust gives purpose room to move. The good fortune of dignity is ease without defenses.

lines.text: Heaven helps him from on high: good fortune, nothing unfavorable.
lines.image: The highest good fortune of Great Possession is help from heaven.

core: The situation is full, bright, and widely supported, like the sun high in the sky. The task is to keep plenty from turning into excess by restraining harm and honoring what is right.
plain: You have substantial resources, reach, and momentum. Use them to protect what is good and stop what is corrupt, while staying aligned with timing rather than forcing outcomes. Prosperity lasts when power remains measured.
advice: Use abundance to curb harm and strengthen what is worthy.

name: 地山謙
summary: High within, low without; strength kept humble
judgment: Modesty: success; the person of integrity brings things to completion.
tuan: Modesty brings success. The way of heaven descends to nourish and shines; the way of earth stays low and moves upward. Heaven empties the full and adds to the modest; earth transforms the full and flows into the modest; spirits harm the full and bless the modest; human beings dislike the full and love the modest. Modesty makes the honored brighter, and makes the lowly impossible to overstep: this is the completion of the person of integrity.
xiang: Within the earth there is a mountain: Modesty. The person of integrity takes from the abundant and gives to the sparse, weighs things, and evens out what is given.

lines.text: Modest and ever more modest, the person of integrity may cross the great river: good fortune.
lines.image: Modest and ever more modest means governing oneself by staying low.

lines.text: Modesty rings out: steadfastness brings good fortune.
lines.image: Modesty rings out and steadfastness brings good fortune because the center has found it.

lines.text: The person of integrity is modest despite toil and brings things to completion: good fortune.
lines.image: Modest despite toil, the person of integrity wins the service of the multitude.

lines.text: Nothing unfavorable: carried-through modesty.
lines.image: Nothing unfavorable in carried-through modesty because it does not violate the rule.

lines.text: He is not enriched by his neighbors; it is favorable to use a punitive expedition: nothing unfavorable.
lines.image: Favorable to use a punitive expedition means marching against those who do not submit.

lines.text: Modesty rings out: favorable to set the army in motion and punish the city and domain.
lines.image: Modesty rings out, yet the aim is not yet gained; the army may be used to punish the city and domain.

core: Real substance is present, but it is kept under a low profile. Modesty here is active fairness: lower yourself, level imbalances, and let merit speak.
plain: Hold confidence inside and restraint outside. Reduce what is excessive, supply what is lacking, and do not display your strength before it is needed. Lasting results come from finishing quietly and justly.
advice: Take from excess, give to lack, and keep your height hidden.

name: 雷地豫
summary: Joy moving with season and momentum
judgment: Enthusiasm: favorable to establish a lord and set the army in motion.
tuan: In Enthusiasm, the firm is answered and its aim moves forward; obedience moves, and that is Enthusiasm. Enthusiasm moves in accord, so even heaven and earth are like this—how much more establishing a lord and setting an army in motion! When heaven and earth move in accord, sun and moon do not overshoot and the four seasons do not err. When the sage moves in accord, punishments become clear and the people submit. Great indeed is the meaning of Enthusiasm in its time!
xiang: Thunder bursts forth from the earth: Enthusiasm. The ancient kings made music to honor virtue, offering it generously to the Highest and matching it with the ancestors.

lines.text: Proclaiming enthusiasm: misfortune.
lines.image: At the first six, proclaiming enthusiasm means the drive is already spent; misfortune.

lines.text: Firm as a stone, before the day is over: steadfastness brings good fortune.
lines.image: Before the day is over, steadfastness brings good fortune because he stands centered and correct.

lines.text: Looking up greedily for joy brings regret; delaying brings regret too.
lines.image: Looking up for joy brings regret because the position is not proper.

lines.text: The source of enthusiasm: great gain. Do not doubt; friends gather like hairpins.
lines.image: As the source of enthusiasm there is great gain, because the aim is carried out on a large scale.

lines.text: Steadfast in illness, enduring and not dying.
lines.image: The six in the fifth is ill yet steadfast because it rides above the firm; enduring without dying because the center is not lost.

lines.text: Darkened enthusiasm: if something has been formed, change it; no blame.
lines.image: Darkened enthusiasm at the top—how could it last long?

core: Energy rises easily and wants to become public joy, music, and coordinated action. It works when the movement follows the season; it fails when pleasure is proclaimed too early or indulged too late.
plain: Use enthusiasm to organize people and set force in order, but watch for overexcitement. Do not confuse loudness with timing; act when support is real, and stop before pleasure turns blind. Good order keeps joy useful.
advice: Move only when excitement matches the moment; cut off indulgence early.

name: 澤雷隨
judgment: Following: Primordial success, prosperity, correctness. There is no blame.
tuan: Following. The strong comes and the weak descends; movement brings joy, and there is following. Great success requires correctness; there is no blame, and all under heaven follow according to the times. How great and significant the meaning of following at the right time is!
xiang: Thunder in the marsh. This is the image of Following. The superior person withdraws by evening and rests at the appointed time.

lines.text: The official changes his course. Correctness is auspicious. Leaving home and engaging with others brings success.
lines.image: The official changes his course because he returns to correctness. Leaving home and engaging with others brings success without losing the right way.

lines.text: One is attached to a young boy and loses the man who should be her partner.
lines.image: Being attached to a young boy means she cannot also remain united with her proper partner.

lines.text: One is attached to her husband and loses the young boy. Following brings what one seeks; it is beneficial to remain correct.
lines.image: Being attached to her husband means she has chosen to abandon the lower attachment.

lines.text: Following brings gains, but correctness brings misfortune. If one is sincere and acts with clarity, what blame can there be?
lines.image: Gains gained by following make the meaning dangerous. Sincerity and clarity along the right path bring merit.

lines.text: Sincere trust in goodness is auspicious.
lines.image: Sincere trust in goodness is auspicious because the position is correct and balanced.

lines.text: One is restrained and bound, and the king goes to offer sacrifice at the western mountain.
lines.image: Being restrained and bound shows that the extreme position has reached its end.

core: Following requires adapting to changing circumstances while remaining true to what is right. Yield to sound guidance, but avoid arbitrary domination.
plain: This situation calls for cooperation and responsiveness rather than rigid control. Adjust your plans as conditions change and follow trustworthy guidance without surrendering your own judgment.
advice: Adapt to changing conditions without abandoning your principles.

name: 山風蠱
en: Work on What Has Been Spoiled
judgment: Work on What Has Been Spoiled: Primordial success. It is beneficial to cross the great water. Three days before the jia day and three days after it.
tuan: Work on What Has Been Spoiled. The strong is above and the weak below; the wind penetrates and then stops, producing the condition of corruption. Work on What Has Been Spoiled brings primordial success, and all under heaven are thereby ordered. It is beneficial to cross the great water because there is work to be done. Three days before the jia day and three days after it: there is an end and then a beginning, the way of heaven.
xiang: Wind beneath the mountain. This is the image of Work on What Has Been Spoiled. The superior person shakes the people into vigor and cultivates virtue.

lines.text: One works to repair the father's corruption. If there is a worthy son, the deceased father is without blame; though dangerous, the end is auspicious.
lines.image: Repairing the father's corruption shows a desire to continue the father's worthy undertaking.

lines.text: One works to repair the mother's corruption. One must not remain rigid.
lines.image: Repairing the mother's corruption follows the middle way.

lines.text: One works to repair the father's corruption. There may be some obscurity, but there is no great blame.
lines.image: Repairing the father's corruption will ultimately be free of blame.

lines.text: One merely eases the father's corruption. Going forward brings regret.
lines.image: Merely easing the father's corruption means going forward without finding a proper solution.

lines.text: One works to repair the father's corruption and thereby earns praise.
lines.image: Repairing the father's corruption and earning praise means carrying it on through virtue.

lines.text: One does not serve kings and nobles, but remains lofty in one's purpose.
lines.image: Not serving kings and nobles shows that one's aspirations can be realized.

core: Existing conditions have decayed and require active repair. Address the inherited problems directly, prepare carefully, and restore soundness through sustained effort.
plain: Something has fallen into disorder and cannot be fixed by waiting alone. Identify what has spoiled, make the necessary corrections before they spread, and persist until the situation is sound.
advice: Identify the underlying damage and begin repairing it systematically.

name: 地澤臨
judgment: Approach: Primordial success, prosperity, benefit, and correctness. By the eighth month, there will be danger.
tuan: Approach. The strong grows increasingly and spreads; there is joy and compliance. The strong is balanced and responds. Great success through correctness is the way of heaven. By the eighth month, there will be danger, because what is waning will not last long.
xiang: The earth is above the marsh. This is the image of Approach. The superior person teaches with inexhaustible thought and protects the people without boundary.

lines.text: A sincere approach. Correctness is auspicious.
lines.image: A sincere approach and correctness are auspicious because the intention is to act rightly.

lines.text: A sincere approach is auspicious, with nothing unfavorable.
lines.image: A sincere approach is auspicious and nothing is unfavorable because it accords with the mandate.

lines.text: An indulgent approach brings no benefit. Once one becomes aware of this, there is no blame.
lines.image: An indulgent approach is unprofitable because the position is unsuitable. Once one becomes aware of it, blame will not persist.

lines.text: A close approach brings no blame.
lines.image: A close approach brings no blame because the position is appropriate.

lines.text: An informed approach is fitting for a great ruler and is auspicious.
lines.image: What is fitting for a great ruler is called the way of balanced action.

lines.text: A sincere and generous approach is auspicious and brings no blame.
lines.image: The auspiciousness of a sincere approach lies in its inner purpose.

core: A position of influence should be used to teach, support, and protect others. Maintain correctness while recognizing that favorable conditions can change.
plain: You have an opportunity to influence and care for those below you. Use that position through sound teaching and genuine support, but stay alert because today’s strength may weaken.
advice: Lead through support and guidance while staying alert to change.

name: 風地觀
judgment: Contemplation: The hands are washed, but no offering is presented. There is reverent sincerity.
tuan: A great perspective is above; below, there is compliance and gentleness. Through balance and correctness, one observes all under heaven: this is Contemplation. The hands are washed, but no offering is presented. There is reverent sincerity, and those below observe and are transformed. One observes the mysterious way of heaven, and the four seasons never falter. The sages use the mysterious way of heaven to establish teachings, and all under heaven submit.
xiang: Wind moves over the earth. This is the image of Contemplation. The former kings inspected the regions, observed the people, and established teachings.

lines.text: A child's way of looking. There is no blame for the ordinary person, but the superior person feels regret.
lines.image: A child's way of looking is the way of an ordinary person.

lines.text: To peer is to observe. For a woman, correctness is beneficial, but the behavior is also disgraceful.
lines.image: Peering to observe may be correct for a woman, but it is still shameful.

lines.text: Observe how I live and move forward or withdraw accordingly.
lines.image: Observing how one lives in order to govern one's advance and retreat has not departed from the right way.

lines.text: Observe the light of the kingdom. It is beneficial to become a guest of the king.
lines.image: Observing the light of the kingdom shows esteem for welcoming worthy guests.

lines.text: Observe how I live. The superior person has no blame.
lines.image: Observing how one lives means observing the people.

lines.text: Observe how the people live. The superior person has no blame.
lines.image: Observing how the people live shows that the aspiration remains unfulfilled.

core: Effective leadership begins with observing conditions, people, and established patterns before acting. Influence others by example and by teaching that leads to transformation.
plain: Look carefully before deciding, and observe how people actually behave rather than relying on appearances. A clear example, combined with sound teaching, can move those below you toward better conduct.
advice: Observe conditions and established patterns before choosing your course.

name: 火雷噬嗑
judgment: Biting Through: Success. It is useful to bring legal disputes to trial.
tuan: There is something in the jaws, which is called Biting Through. Biting through brings success: the rigid and the yielding are divided, and movement brings clarity. Thunder and lightning combine to reveal a pattern. The yielding line occupies the central position and rises above; though it is not in its proper place, it is useful to bring legal disputes to trial.
xiang: Thunder and lightning bite through. The ancient kings used this to clarify penalties and strengthen the law.

lines.text: You wear fetters that cut off your toes. There is no blame.
lines.image: Wearing fetters that cut off your toes means you cannot move.

lines.text: You bite through soft flesh, and your nose disappears. There is no blame.
lines.image: Biting through soft flesh and losing your nose comes from riding over the strong.

lines.text: You bite through dried meat and encounter poison. There is slight distress, but no blame.
lines.image: Encountering poison is due to your position being improper.

lines.text: You bite through dried meat and obtain a metal arrow. It is beneficial to persevere through hardship. Good fortune.
lines.image: The benefit of perseverance and good fortune in hardship is that your brilliance is not yet fully recognized.

lines.text: You bite through dried meat and obtain gold. Persevere despite danger, and there will be no blame.
lines.image: Persevering despite danger is blameless because you have obtained what is proper.

lines.text: You are loaded with fetters that cut off your ears. This is ominous.
lines.image: Fetters that cut off your ears mean that your hearing is no longer clear.

core: Obstacles must be broken through decisively, but force must be balanced with flexibility. Progress depends on resolving disputes clearly and acting with determination.
plain: This situation calls for cutting through a stubborn obstruction rather than avoiding it. Use firm procedures, judgment, and fair enforcement, while adapting your approach to the resistance you encounter. Persistence is necessary, but brute force alone is not.
advice: Resolve the blockage through clear evidence, firm procedure, and steady action.

name: 山火賁
judgment: Grace: Success. There is small benefit in going somewhere.
tuan: Grace brings success. The yielding comes and adorns the strong, and therefore there is success. The strong above divides and adorns the yielding, so there is small benefit in going somewhere; this is the pattern of heaven. Civilization restrains, and this is the pattern of humanity. Observe the patterns of heaven to understand the changes of the seasons; observe the patterns of humanity to transform the world.
xiang: Fire lies below the mountain: this is Grace. The superior person uses clarity to govern all affairs and does not dare to make judgments lightly.

lines.text: You adorn your feet and leave the carriage to walk.
lines.image: Leaving the carriage to walk means righteousness does not permit you to ride.

lines.text: You adorn your beard.
lines.image: Adorning your beard means you wish to rise together with the superior.

lines.text: You are adorned as if soaked with water. To persevere forever brings good fortune.
lines.image: The good fortune of persevering forever is that no one can insult you in the end.

lines.text: You are adorned, bright and plain. A white horse comes at a gallop. They are not robbers but those who come to make a marriage alliance.
lines.image: The sixth line is in its proper place, yet there is doubt. They are not robbers but come to make a marriage alliance; in the end, there will no blame.

lines.text: You adorn the mound and garden. The bundle of silk is modest. There is distress, but in the end there is good fortune.
lines.image: The good fortune of the sixth line brings joy.

lines.text: Your adornment is plain white. There is no blame.
lines.image: Plain white adornment is blameless because the superior line achieves its aspiration.

core: Adornment can reveal inner worth, but it should clarify rather than conceal reality. Careful presentation helps, provided judgment remains sound and proportionate.
plain: The situation calls for refinement and thoughtful presentation, not empty show. Make the substance clear and let form support it, while avoiding judgments made from appearances alone. Even modest beauty or courtesy can lead to favorable results when used appropriately.
advice: Present your best qualities clearly without disguising the substance.

name: 山地剝
summary: Yield to the turn of decline
judgment: Splitting Apart: It is not beneficial to go somewhere.
tuan: Splitting Apart means that the yielding changes the strong. It is not beneficial to go somewhere because the petty person grows powerful. Follow and stop; observe the pattern. The superior person honors the ebb and flow, the fullness and emptiness of things, for this is the way of heaven.
xiang: The mountain rests upon the earth: this is Splitting Apart. The superior uses this to give support below and provide a secure dwelling.

lines.text: The bed is split apart at the foot. You disregard correctness. This is ominous.
lines.image: Splitting the bed at the foot destroys what lies below.

lines.text: The bed is split apart at the edge. You disregard correctness. This is ominous.
lines.image: Splitting the bed at the edge comes from having no support.

lines.text: You split it apart. There is no blame.
lines.image: Splitting it apart without blame means losing connection with those above and below.

lines.text: The bed is split apart at the flesh. This is ominous.
lines.image: Splitting the bed at the flesh means disaster is drawing close.

lines.text: You string the fish in order. By favoring the palace attendants, nothing is unfavorable.
lines.image: Favoring the palace attendants brings no blame in the end.

lines.text: The large fruit is not eaten. The superior gains the people's support, while the petty person strips away the house.
lines.image: The superior gains support because the people bear him. The petty person strips away the house and remains unusable in the end.

core: Conditions are decaying, and attempts to advance are vulnerable to worsening. The wisdom lies in recognizing the decline, conserving what remains, and stopping before it turns destructive.
plain: The present situation is stripping away strength and exposing what cannot endure. Do not force progress or rely on the powerful to protect you. Wait, support those beneath you, and preserve a secure foundation until conditions change.
advice: Stop advancing, protect your foundation, and wait for the decline to pass.

name: 地雷復
judgment: Return: Success. Coming and going bring no illness. Friends come without blame. The cycle repeats, and after seven days it returns, so it is beneficial to go somewhere.
tuan: Return brings success. The strong returns, and movement proceeds in accordance with what is right, so coming and going bring no illness and friends come without blame. The cycle repeats, and after seven days it returns: this is the way of heaven. It is beneficial to go somewhere because the strong grows. Is this what returning reveals as the heart of heaven and earth?
xiang: Thunder lies within the earth: this is Return. The ancient kings closed the passes at the winter solstice, so merchants and travelers did not go out, and the ruler did not inspect the various regions.

lines.text: You do not go far before returning, and have hardly any regret. Great good fortune.
lines.image: Returning before going far is the way to cultivate oneself.

lines.text: You rest in the return. Good fortune.
lines.image: The good fortune of resting in the return comes from allowing benevolence to grow below.

lines.text: You return again and again. There is danger, but no blame.
lines.image: The danger of repeated return is not blameful because it accords with what is right.

lines.text: You return alone in the middle of the way.
lines.image: Returning alone in the middle follows the proper way.

lines.text: Your return is sincere and earnest. There is no regret.
lines.image: A sincere return brings no regret because you examine yourself inwardly.

lines.text: You are lost in return and do not return. This is ominous and brings disaster. If you use it to send an army, there will be a great defeat, and your ruler will be in danger. For ten years you will not be able to campaign.
lines.image: The misfortune of being lost in return comes from turning against the ruler’s way.

core: A new beginning is emerging through a natural cycle of return. The favorable path is to turn back early, recover what is right, and move forward only when renewal has taken hold.
plain: This is a time to return to a sound path, retrace past mistakes, and renew your direction. Progress becomes beneficial once the return has settled into a stable rhythm. Impatience and repeated deviation can turn a promising recovery into disaster.
advice: Return early to the right path, steady yourself, and renew before advancing.

name: 天雷無妄
judgment: Innocence: It is favorable to the beginning, to prosper, and to be steadfast. If one is not upright, there will be mistakes, and it is not favorable to have somewhere to go.
tuan: Innocence. The strong comes from outside and becomes the master within. Movement is vigorous; the strong occupies the center and responds to what is below. Great success comes through rectitude: this is Heaven’s command. If one is not upright, there will be mistakes, and it is not favorable to have somewhere to go. Where can one go under the condition of innocence? Heaven does not grant its aid. Go, and you will meet disaster.
xiang: Under Heaven, thunder moves, and all things receive without falseness. The former kings made abundant offerings in response to the seasons and nurtured all things.

lines.text: If you go forward without falseness, it is favorable.
lines.image: Going forward without falseness brings the fulfillment of one’s aspirations.

lines.text: If you do not plow in hopes of a harvest, nor cultivate new fields for food, it is favorable to have somewhere to go.
lines.image: Without plowing for a harvest or cultivating new fields, one has not yet become wealthy.

lines.text: The disaster of innocence: a cow may be tied up, and a passerby may take it, but it becomes the disaster of the people of the town.
lines.image: The passerby gains the cow, while the people of the town suffer the loss.

lines.text: It can be held steady and correct, without blame.
lines.image: Holding firm in correctness and avoiding blame is the natural course.

lines.text: An illness without falseness needs no medicine and brings joy.
lines.image: The medicine for a trouble of innocence must not be tried.

lines.text: If you travel without falseness, there will be mistakes, and nothing will be favorable.
lines.image: Traveling without falseness leads to disaster at the end of the road.

core: Innocence means acting without deceit, without contrivance, and with complete sincerity. It requires following the natural course of things rather than manipulating outcomes.
plain: This situation favors honest, straightforward action and unexpected good fortune. Falsehood or distorted motives will bring mistakes, while trying to force a result will undermine you. Let sincerity and the natural order guide your conduct.
advice: Act transparently and let genuine effort determine the result.

name: 山天大畜
judgment: Great Taming: It is favorable to be steadfast and correct. It is favorable not to eat at home, and favorable to cross the great river.
tuan: Great Taming. The strong is vigorous and substantial, its brilliance renewing itself each day. Its virtue is strong in the upward and honors the worthy. To be able to stop the vigorous is greatly correct. Not eating at home is favorable because it nurtures the worthy. It is favorable to cross the great river because this responds to Heaven.
xiang: Heaven is within the mountain: this is Great Taming. The superior person broadens his knowledge of former sayings and past conduct, thereby accumulating virtue.

lines.text: There is danger, but it is favorable to stop where you are.
lines.image: Recognizing danger and stopping keeps you from encountering disaster.

lines.text: The spokes come loose from the carriage wheel.
lines.image: When the spokes loosen from the wheel, there is no blame in the center.

lines.text: A strong horse runs in pursuit; it is favorable to endure hardship and remain steadfast. Keep the carriage at rest and guard it. It is favorable to have somewhere to go.
lines.image: The prospect of going forward accords with the higher purpose.

lines.text: A young calf is restrained by a crossbar: it is greatly favorable.
lines.image: The great good fortune of the fourth line brings joy.

lines.text: A boar’s tusk is restrained: it is favorable.
lines.image: The good fortune of the fifth line brings celebration.

lines.text: How broad is Heaven’s road! It is favorable.
lines.image: The broad road of Heaven means the great way is widely practiced.

core: Great Taming calls for gathering and storing strength while restraining excessive movement. It rewards patient preparation, disciplined learning, and readiness to act when the time comes.
plain: You need to build up your resources instead of rushing ahead. Discipline your strength, learn from the past, and identify worthy people whose support can advance a larger undertaking. When conditions are ready, crossing major obstacles becomes favorable.
advice: Build your reserves now, then act when the right conditions arrive.

name: 山雷頤
judgment: Nourishment: Steadfastness and correctness bring good fortune. Observe how others are nourished, and seek your own food.
tuan: Nourishment. Steadfastness and correctness bring good fortune; nourishing what is correct brings good fortune. Observe nourishment and observe what those people nurture. Seek your own food and observe how people nourish themselves. Heaven and Earth nourish all things; the sages nourish the worthy and, through them, the myriad people. The meaning and timeliness of Nourishment are indeed great.
xiang: There is thunder below the mountain: this is Nourishment. The superior person is careful in speech and moderate in food and drink.

lines.text: Set aside your spiritual tortoise and stare at my moving jaws: it is ominous.
lines.image: Watching my moving jaws is no reason to value oneself.

lines.text: You turn your head toward nourishment, contrary to the proper way, and look toward the hill for nourishment. Journeying brings misfortune.
lines.image: The second line’s misfortune in journeying comes from traveling apart from its proper kind.

lines.text: You frustrate nourishment. Steadfastness brings misfortune. Do not act for ten years; nothing is favorable.
lines.image: Doing nothing for ten years means the way is greatly contradicted.

lines.text: You turn your head toward nourishment: it is favorable. The tiger watches intently, eager to pursue its prey, but there is no blame.
lines.image: The good fortune of turning toward nourishment comes from bestowing light from above.

lines.text: You contradict the proper way, but remain steadfast and correct, which is favorable. Do not cross the great river.
lines.image: Remaining steadfast brings good fortune through harmonious obedience to what is above.

lines.text: You provide nourishment from above. Even amid danger, it is favorable. It is favorable to cross the great river.
lines.image: Nourishing from above despite danger brings great celebration.

core: Nourishment concerns what sustains people, what one seeks to sustain, and whether that nourishment is sound. Integrity requires disciplined speech, moderate appetites, and care over how others are supported.
plain: Examine what you and others are sustaining, including the sources of your livelihood and the needs of those around you. Speak carefully, avoid excess, and build support on principles rather than appetite.
advice: Moderate your speech and appetites while supporting what is right.

name: 澤風大過
judgment: Preponderance of the Great: The ridgepole bends. It is favorable to have somewhere to go, and it is favorable.
tuan: Preponderance of the Great. What is great has gone too far. The ridgepole bends because its ends are weak. The strong has exceeded its proper place but remains in the center; yielding yet moving with pleasure. It is favorable to have somewhere to go, and only then is it favorable. The meaning and timeliness of Preponderance of the Great are indeed great.
xiang: The marsh swallows up the tree: this is Preponderance of the Great. The superior person stands alone without fear and withdraws from the world without distress.

lines.text: Use white rushes as a mat. There is no blame.
lines.image: Using white rushes as a mat shows that the yielding element lies below.

lines.text: A withered poplar sprouts shoots; an old man takes a young wife as his wife. Nothing is unfavorable.
lines.image: An old man and a young wife are joined in an unusual way through excess.

lines.text: The ridgepole bends: it is ominous.
lines.image: The misfortune of a bending ridgepole means it cannot be supported from below.

lines.text: The ridgepole rises high: it is favorable, but there will be another difficulty.
lines.image: The good fortune of the ridgepole remaining high is that it does not bend downward.

lines.text: A withered poplar blossoms; an old woman takes a mature husband as her husband. There is neither blame nor praise.
lines.image: How can a withered poplar keep blooming long? An old woman with a mature husband is also unsightly.

lines.text: In excessive crossing, the waves swallow your head: it is ominous, but there is no blame.
lines.image: The misfortune of excessive crossing cannot be blamed, because the situation is beyond ordinary control.

core: This situation places extraordinary pressure on the structure that supports everything. The central members remain sound, but the ends are weak, so action must be exceptional and carefully measured.
plain: The main supports are bearing more than they should, leaving the foundation vulnerable. You may need to act boldly, but not by ignoring the weak points or relying on unsupported assistance. Recognize when extraordinary measures are truly required.
advice: Support the weakest points before attempting any exceptional move.

name: 坎為水
summary: Repeated danger demands trust and careful movement
judgment: The Abysmal: repeated danger. If you keep your heart sincere, you will prevail. Action will be honored.
tuan: The Abysmal means repeated danger. Water flows on and on without filling the pit; you move through danger without losing your trustworthiness. You prevail because you remain firm at the center. Action will be honored because going forward brings achievement. Heaven's danger cannot be climbed; earth's danger consists of mountains, rivers, hills, and ridges. Rulers establish defenses to protect their states. How great the use of danger in the proper time!
xiang: Water comes again and again, making the Abysmal. Thus the superior person maintains constant virtue and practices what has been taught.

lines.text: Repeated danger: you enter the deep pit. It is unlucky.
lines.image: Entering the pit in repeated danger means losing the proper way; this is unlucky.

lines.text: There is danger in the pit, but seeking something small brings limited gain.
lines.image: Seeking a small gain means you have not yet emerged from the center.

lines.text: You come and fall into danger upon danger. The danger is great, and you are trapped. Do not act.
lines.image: Coming and falling into danger upon danger will bring no achievement in the end.

lines.text: A jar of wine, two vessels of food, and an earthen pot. Make your offering simple and pass it through the window. In the end, there will be no blame.
lines.image: The jar of wine and two food vessels show the meeting of strength and gentleness.

lines.text: The pit is not yet full, and the waters have become level. There will be no blame.
lines.image: The pit is not full because the center has not yet reached fullness.

lines.text: You are bound with cords and put among the thorny bushes. For three years you cannot get free. This is unlucky.
lines.image: The highest line has lost the proper way; its misfortune lasts three years.

core: The Abysmal consists of danger upon danger and repeated pitfalls. Trust, steadiness, and careful conduct are needed to move through it without losing your way.
plain: You are facing difficult and dangerous conditions, possibly several obstacles in succession. Keep your commitments, remain centered, and act with care rather than forcing progress. Help may come, but only if you preserve sincerity and reliability.
advice: Face one danger at a time and keep your word.

name: 離為火
summary: Rely on clarity and steady devotion
judgment: The Clinging: it is beneficial and correct to succeed. Raise cows. This is auspicious.
tuan: The Clinging means attachment. The sun and moon are attached to heaven; the hundred grains and grasses are attached to the earth. Double brightness attached to the correct order transforms and completes the world. The gentle attaches itself to the central and correct, and therefore succeeds. This is why raising cows is auspicious.
xiang: Two lights arise: this is the Clinging. Thus the great person continues the light and shines it upon the four directions.

lines.text: You tread on uneven ground. Respect it, and there will be no blame.
lines.image: Respecting the uneven ground helps you avoid blame.

lines.text: The yellow light is clinging. It is greatly auspicious.
lines.image: The yellow light is greatly auspicious because it follows the middle way.

lines.text: The light of the setting sun. If you do not beat a pot and sing, you will lament the approach of great old age. This is unlucky.
lines.image: The light of the setting sun cannot endure for long.

lines.text: It comes suddenly, burns like a fire, kills like death, and is discarded like something worthless.
lines.image: What comes suddenly has nowhere to be received.

lines.text: Tears flow freely, and grief and lamentation arise. This is auspicious.
lines.image: The auspiciousness of the sixth line, in the fifth place, comes from its attachment to the ruler and nobles.

lines.text: The king goes out to campaign. There is praise. He cuts off the head and captures the rebels. There will be no blame.
lines.image: The king campaigns to set the kingdom right.

core: Clarity and warmth depend on what they attach themselves to. Attach yourself to what is correct, remain humble, and preserve a steady course.
plain: The Clinging points to connection through light, awareness, and devotion. It favors relationships and enterprises supported by sincerity, moderation, and a clear moral center. Avoid dependence that consumes your independence or blinds you to approaching decline.
advice: Attach yourself to what is clear, correct, and sustaining.

name: 澤山咸
summary: Mutual attraction through openness and sincerity
judgment: Influence: success. It is beneficial and correct to marry. This is auspicious.
tuan: Influence means mutual attraction. The gentle above and the strong below, the two forces, influence each other and give one another support. Rest brings delight, as the man comes beneath the woman. Therefore there is success, benefit, and correctness; marriage is auspicious. Heaven and earth influence each other, and all things are born and transformed. Sages influence people's hearts, and the world becomes peaceful. Observe what they influence, and the true nature of heaven, earth, and all things becomes visible.
xiang: A lake lies above the mountain: this is Influence. Thus the superior person receives others with an open mind.

lines.text: Your attraction reaches your big toe.
lines.image: Attraction reaches the big toe because the intention is directed outward.

lines.text: Your attraction reaches your calf. It is unlucky to move, but auspicious to remain still.
lines.image: Although there is misfortune in moving, remaining still is auspicious because it avoids harm.

lines.text: Your attraction reaches your thigh. You cling to what follows you, and going forward brings difficulty.
lines.image: Attraction reaching the thigh means you have not found a settled place. The intention is to follow others, and what you cling to is low.

lines.text: Correctness brings good fortune, and regret disappears. If you rush back and forth uneasily, friends will follow your thoughts.
lines.image: Correctness brings good fortune and removes regret because you have not yet been harmed by influence. Restless movement shows that your influence is not yet broad and bright.

lines.text: Your attraction reaches your back flesh. There will be no regret.
lines.image: Attraction reaches the back flesh because your intention is restrained.

lines.text: Your attraction reaches your jaws, cheeks, and tongue.
lines.image: Attraction reaching the jaws, cheeks, and tongue means there is only empty talk.

core: Influence arises when people genuinely respond to one another. Openness, shared feeling, and respectful mutual attraction create harmony, but impulsive attachment does not.
plain: This situation calls for authentic connection rather than manipulation. Be receptive, listen to what others feel, and allow mutual response to develop naturally. Strong attraction can still be mishandled if it becomes restless, possessive, or blind to proper timing.
advice: Respond sincerely, but let attachment grow without urgency.

name: 雷風恆
judgment: Duration: success, without blame. It is beneficial and correct to have somewhere to go.
tuan: Duration means lasting. Strength is above, and gentleness below. Thunder and wind move together, yielding and in motion; strength and gentleness correspond to one another. This is duration. Duration brings success, without blame, and is beneficial and correct because it means remaining long on the proper way. The way of heaven and earth endures without end. It is beneficial to have somewhere to go because the end returns to the beginning. The sun and moon receive heaven's power and can shine forever; the four seasons change and can bring lasting completion. Sages remain long on their way, and the world is transformed and completed. Observe what they sustain, and the true nature of heaven, earth, and all things becomes visible.
xiang: Thunder and wind: this is Duration. Thus the superior person establishes a direction and does not change it.

lines.text: You seek too deeply too soon in duration. Correctness here is unlucky, and there is nothing beneficial.
lines.image: The misfortune of seeking depth too soon comes from trying to reach deep waters at the beginning.

lines.text: Regret disappears.
lines.image: The second line's regret disappears because it can remain long in the middle.

lines.text: If you do not keep your virtue constant, you may bear shame. Even correctness brings difficulty.
lines.image: If you do not keep your virtue constant, there is nowhere that can receive you.

lines.text: There are no birds in the field.
lines.image: If you remain long in a position that is not right, how could birds come?

lines.text: Keep your virtue constant and correct. For a woman this is auspicious; for a man it is unlucky.
lines.image: A woman's constant correctness is auspicious because she follows one course to the end. For a man to follow the woman is shameful and creates misfortune.

lines.text: You disturb constancy at the top. This is unlucky.
lines.image: Disturbing constancy in the highest place brings no achievement.

core: Duration is the power of sustained commitment to a proper direction. Lasting achievement comes from steady practice, not from rigid attachment to one method or an attempt to force depth too soon.
plain: A long-term effort is favorable when its direction is sound. Keep your commitments and establish routines that can endure. At the same time, persistence should not become obstinacy; review methods and circumstances without abandoning your central purpose.
advice: Choose a sound direction, then sustain it consistently.

name: 天山遯
judgment: Retreat. Success. The small advantage lies in perseverance.
tuan: Retreat brings success because one who withdraws at the right time can still prosper. The strong line occupies its proper place and responds to its counterpart, moving in accord with the times. The small advantage of perseverance grows gradually. The meaning of retreat in its proper season is indeed great.
xiang: A mountain rises beneath heaven: this is Retreat. The superior person keeps distance from petty people without hating them, and maintains dignity through reserve.

lines.text: Retreat at the rear, with danger. Do not proceed anywhere.
lines.image: The danger of being last to retreat disappears if you do not go on.

lines.text: It is held fast by yellow oxhide; no one can release it.
lines.image: Being held by yellow oxhide means the resolve is firm.

lines.text: Tied in retreat; illness brings danger. Keeping servants and concubines is favorable.
lines.image: The danger of being tied in retreat comes from illness and exhaustion. Keeping servants and concubines is favorable, but great matters cannot be undertaken.

lines.text: Delight in retreat. It is favorable for the superior person, but not for the petty one.
lines.image: The superior person delights in retreat; the petty person cannot.

lines.text: A fine retreat. Perseverance brings good fortune.
lines.image: A fine and upright retreat preserves the right intention.

lines.text: A generous retreat. Nothing is unfavorable.
lines.image: A generous retreat is untroubled and leaves nothing to doubt.

core: Retreat is necessary when conditions turn against you, especially after a period of strength. Move carefully, avoid unnecessary exposure, and preserve your principles while waiting for the right opening.
plain: This situation calls for a strategic withdrawal rather than a head-on confrontation. Distinguish yourself from harmful people through restraint and firm boundaries, not hostility. Preserve your position and reconsider your move once conditions become clearer.
advice: Withdraw from the immediate conflict and wait for better conditions.

name: 雷天大壯
judgment: Great Power. Perseverance is beneficial.
tuan: Great Power means that the powerful are strong. Strength moving with force produces this power. In Great Power, perseverance is beneficial because the powerful are upright. When righteousness and greatness are visible, the feelings of heaven and earth can be seen!
xiang: Thunder moves in heaven: this is Great Power. The superior person does not tread beyond what is proper.

lines.text: Strength begins in the toes. Moving forward brings danger, though sincerity remains.
lines.image: Strength shown in the toes leaves no room for genuine trust to develop.

lines.text: Perseverance brings good fortune.
